title: Voice chat
lede: How to talk to the coding agent hands-free through headphones. Audio stays on your machine; only the agent call goes out.

check.name: Check and install
check.role: A built-in check reports what is missing; install it and re-run until clean.
details: node scripts/voice/voice-loop.ts --check prints the speech model, voice backend, platform, recorder and player.

more: Linux or WSL: apt install sox espeak-ng pulseaudio-utils, plus whisper-cli on PATH.
Download the ggml-base.en Whisper model once.

voice.name: Pick a voice
voice.role: Choose how replies are spoken, or leave it on auto.
details: auto tries Piper, then macOS say, then espeak-ng.
XTTS clones a voice from a sample of about 6 seconds; it is the richest and heaviest, needs Python, and is never picked automatically.

head: Variable
Default
What
rows: spoken lines, to give the loop a persona

launch.name: Launch
launch.role: Start the loop with Claude by default, or Codex.
details: Set VOICE_AGENT=codex for Codex, on both --check and launch.
risks: The runner speaks only the Claude and Codex CLI protocols; never swap in another binary while keeping their flags.

turn.name: Each turn
turn.role: Your speech is recorded, transcribed, answered by the agent, and read back aloud.

more: Mic, then a sox silence gate, then a wav file.
whisper.cpp turns it into text, locally.
The Claude or Codex CLI replies; this is the only remote call.
Text-to-speech plays the reply in your headphones, locally.

details: No push-to-talk: the silence gate starts and stops recording by sound level.
risks: Headphones are assumed so the agent's voice never re-enters the mic.
qs: Which account and billing does the agent call use?

stop.name: Stop
stop.role: Quit with Ctrl-C or by saying an exit phrase.
details: Exit phrases: "stop listening", "goodbye agent", "that's all for now".

gate.d: Starts and stops recording by sound level, so there is no push-to-talk.

whisper.d: A local speech-recognition program and its model file.

sox.d: A command-line audio tool that records the mic.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand scaffold's /voice-chat skill: a hands-free voice loop for talking to a coding agent.
